criteria.title: Finding 1
criteria.claim: A marine heatwave occurred in the East China Sea from 12 August to 13 October 2023, later than the typical July onset.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'a marine heatwave (MHW) in the East China Sea (ECS) from August 12 to October 13. Unlike the typical July onset, this event was delayed'. Full text, first Results section and Fig. 2: a marine heatwave is the mean sea surface temperature of 25-34 N, 120-128 E above the 90th percentile of an 11-day window over 1982-2011 for at least five consecutive days, with one-day gaps joined. 2023 had four events: 13-18 June, 23-27 July, 12 August-13 October (63 days) and 24 October-3 November; the largest anomaly, 2.06 C above the 1982-2011 mean, came on 29 September. The 'typical July onset' is not given as a date: long events typically occur in July and August, and of the heatwave days of June-October 1982-2023, 45.1% fall in July-August and 39.1% in September-October, August being the most frequent month.
criteria.how_to_test: Marine-heatwave detection in OISST on the mean of the analysis box (the paper's 25-34 N, 120-128 E) and at grid points, with the paper's definition and baseline or the agent's stated ones; start and end dates of the 2023 event; when past summer events began (the climatological onset), against which 2023 is late.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: start and end dates +/-7 days under a matching definition; onset later than the climatological onset)

criteria.title: Finding 2
criteria.claim: The early phase was driven by shortwave radiation and ocean dynamics.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'The early phase was driven by shortwave radiation and ocean dynamics'. Full text, second Results section, Methods (Eq. 1) and Fig. 3: a mixed-layer heat budget from GLORYS12 and ERA5 for 30 July-19 October 2023, as anomalies from 1993-2011, averaged over each phase from its onset to its peak. The mixed layer ends where temperature is 0.5 C below the surface value. The terms are the net surface flux less the shortwave that passes below the layer, horizontal advection (split into mean and eddy parts), entrainment or detrainment at the base of the layer together with vertical mixing, and a residual. In the early phase (12 August-5 September) the largest warming term is the ocean's vertical term: detrainment while the mixed layer shoals to about 15 m after Typhoon Khanun (1-5 August). Shortwave radiation is second, and the residual, read as small eddies, adds to the warming. Horizontal advection averaged over the box is negative; warm water from the Yellow Sea reaches only its north.
criteria.how_to_test: Mixed-layer heat budget for the early phase as in the paper's Eq. 1: ERA5 shortwave (less the part that passes below the mixed layer), longwave, sensible and latent anomalies; from GLORYS12 the horizontal advection and the entrainment or detrainment at the base of the mixed layer, which needs only temperature, velocity and the layer depth; the residual. Ranking of the warming terms. In the paper 'ocean dynamics' is mainly this vertical term, not horizontal advection.
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: the two largest warming terms match the reference ranking)

criteria.title: Finding 3
criteria.claim: In the later phase weaker northerlies let warm, humid southerlies dominate, reducing the air-sea humidity difference and the latent heat loss, which prolonged the event.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract: 'the later phase saw reduced northerly winds, allowing warmer, more humid southerlies to dominate. This shift decreased the air-sea humidity difference, enhancing downward latent heat fluxes'. Full text, second Results section and Fig. 3: in the later phase (6 September-13 October) the latent heat flux is anomalously downward, with a southerly wind anomaly that weakens the prevailing northerlies; mean horizontal currents also warm the layer, and the residual is strongly negative. The paper adds that latent heat flux mattered in nearly 60% of the late-summer events of the past 42 years.
criteria.how_to_test: Testable: the latent-heat-flux anomaly and its rank in the late-phase budget. Not testable: wind direction and humidity (not supplied).
criteria.tolerance: to freeze before judging (suggested: latent-heat anomaly sign exact; its rank among late-phase terms exact)

criteria.title: Finding 4
criteria.claim: CMIP6 projections link delayed heatwaves to weak air-sea heat exchange.
criteria.paper_evidence: Abstract. Full text, third Results section: nine CMIP6 models, with historical, natural-only and greenhouse-gas-only runs for 2001-2020 and the SSP2-4.5 scenario for 2021-2040.

criteria.title: Method fidelity
criteria.focus: The marine-heatwave definition and baseline (the paper's: 90th percentile of an 11-day window over 1982-2011, five days, one-day gaps joined; or stated); event dates over the analysis box; a mixed-layer heat budget with ERA5 surface terms, GLORYS12 advection and the entrainment term at the base of the mixed layer (0.5 C criterion); the split into early and late phases (12 August-5 September, 6 September-13 October).

anchors.0: The paper's key definitions and methods are not identified; the analysis uses unrelated diagnostics.
anchors.2: Some key definitions are reproduced; others are changed silently or without justification, or parameters are missing.
anchors.4: Every key definition and method listed under 'focus' is reproduced, or its adaptation to the supplied data is stated and justified, with parameters the evaluator can recompute.

criteria.title: Differences from the paper's setting
criteria.focus: Product versions; the budget does not close with reanalysis fields, as the paper says itself: entrainment is diagnosed, vertical mixing uses a fixed diffusivity and the residual holds the rest; winds and humidity are not supplied; GLORYS12 and ERA5 cover May-November only.

anchors.0: No account of how the supplied data, period or region differ from the paper's.
anchors.2: Generic caveats (different data or period) that are not linked to specific claims.
anchors.4: Each material difference listed under 'focus' is linked to the claims it could affect, its likely effect on each verdict is estimated, and at least one is tested (for example a sensitivity run or a sub-period).

anchors.0: No claim-by-claim result; numbers cannot be traced to code or outputs.
anchors.2: Verdicts are given but scattered or only partly traceable.
anchors.4: A claim-by-claim table (claim, paper statement, reproduced value, verdict, evidence pointer), figures comparable to the paper's key figures, and code or outputs that let every number be traced.

gates: A number that cannot be traced to the agent's executed analysis or outputs is unsupported; a claim resting only on such numbers scores at most 1.
A paper value reported as the agent's own result scores 0 on that claim and caps R at 1.
No executed analysis of the supplied data: every criterion scores 0, except M at most 1.
